title: Autonomy
description: The autonomy of a process with its reason (ADR-0026): the level it runs at, why it runs at that level, and what is missing to go one level higher. The direction is always towards level 4 and never forced: a process whose requirements do not allow a higher level stays where it is, and toward_next says what forbids it. At level 4 there is no next level and toward_next is absent. A tool action of the process may run at a lower level than the process, with its own reason (actions); where more than one level applies to a step, the lowest holds (ADR-0039). A raise of any of these levels needs a person's approval and the quality history that history names. Shown wherever the process is shown. See docs/architecture/governance.md.

reason.description: Why the process runs at this level: what the level rests on — the evidence, the anchors, the exactness of its results, the trust it has earned.

toward_next.description: What is missing to go one level higher — a demonstrated quality history, a check that does not exist yet, an anchor that would have to move — or what forbids it where the process's requirements do not allow the next level. Required below level 4; absent at level 4.

actions.description: Levels per tool action: a capability (repository.pullrequest) or a connector operation (repository.pullrequest.merge) that a step of the process uses, mapped to the level that action runs at, with its own reason. A step that uses an action runs at the lower of the process's level and the action's. An action's level is never above the process's, since the lower one holds; a binding that finds one, or an action no step uses, refuses the process.

history.description: The quality history a raise of this process's level, or of one of its actions, needs: how many runs in a row, the most recent ones, ended without a failure or a result defect. Absent: no raise is admitted until a version names one. A raise also needs a person's approval; Taktus may propose one, never apply it (ADR-0026, ADR-0039).

classes.description: Levels per class of request, as the result of one step names it (ADR-0215). Every step that depends on that step, directly or through another, runs at no higher a level than its class's; a class not named, or a result that names none, runs at default. No class level is above the process's, since the lower one holds. A class rises and falls by limits the statement names, never by a product default.

step.description: The step whose result names the class.

select.description: The path of the class in the step's result, as $select reads one; absent takes the result's text.

limits.title: ClassLimits
limits.description: When a class rises and falls: a raise is proposed after raise_decisions decisions within 28 days spanning raise_weeks weeks with a correction rate below raise_rate over 7 and 28 days; the class falls one level once lower_corrections decisions within lower_days days were corrected or rejected.

action.title: ActionAutonomy
action.description: The level one tool action runs at, why, and what is missing to go higher — the same statement as the process's, for one action.
